title: Problem Overview: Hypergraph Turán Densities
content:
**Erdős Problem #712** asks to determine the Turán density for r-uniform hypergraphs avoiding a complete k-clique K_k^r, for all k > r > 2. The graph case (r=2) was solved by Turán in 1941, but the hypergraph case is completely open — even the simplest case K_4^3 remains unsolved after 80+ years.

Erdős offered a $500 prize for any single case and $1000 for the full solution. This is one of the most famous open problems in extremal combinatorics.
mathContext: The Turán density π_r(K_k^r) = lim_{n→∞} ex_r(n, K_k^r)/C(n,r) measures the maximum edge density achievable while avoiding a complete r-uniform clique on k vertices. For graphs: π_2(K_k) = (1-1/(k-1))/2.

title: r-Uniform Hypergraph and Clique Definitions
content:
**Hypergraph V r** is a structure with edges (a Finset of Finsets) and a uniformity proof that every edge has cardinality r. This generalizes graphs (r=2) to higher uniformities.

**formsClique H S** says every r-subset of S is an edge of H — S forms a complete K_|S|^r.

**isCliqueFree H k** says no k-element subset forms a clique. This is the avoidance condition in the Turán problem.
mathContext: The structure-based approach cleanly separates the hypergraph data (edges) from the uniformity proof, mirroring Mathlib's style for mathematical structures.

title: Hypergraph Turán Number
content:
**turanNumber n r k** is ex_r(n, K_k^r): the maximum number of edges in a K_k^r-free r-uniform hypergraph on n vertices. Defined via sSup (supremum) over all valid hypergraphs.

**turan_upper_trivial** provides the obvious upper bound: ex_r(n, K_k^r) ≤ C(n,r), the total number of r-subsets.

title: Turán Density and Its Properties
content:
**turanDensity r k** = π_r(K_k^r) = lim_{n→∞} ex_r(n,K_k^r)/C(n,r). The normalized limit of Turán numbers as n → ∞.

**turan_density_exists** axiomatizes that this limit exists (a known result). **turan_density_bounds** states 0 ≤ π ≤ 1.
mathContext: The existence of the Turán density as a limit follows from a super-additivity argument (Katona-Nemetz-Simonovits). The density captures the asymptotic edge density of extremal hypergraphs.

title: Classical Turán Theorem (r=2)
content:
**turan_theorem** states the complete solution for graphs: π_2(K_k) = (1-1/(k-1))/2. This classical result (1941) gives both the exact density and the extremal construction (the balanced complete (k-1)-partite graph).

**turan_graph_extremal** gives the exact edge count of the Turán graph T(n,k-1). For k=3: π_2(K_3) = 0, since K_3-free graphs have at most n²/4 edges (Mantel's theorem).
mathContext: Turán's theorem is the foundation of extremal graph theory. The proof combines the double-counting technique with an optimization argument over balanced partitions.

title: The K_4^3 Case: Turán's Conjecture
content:
**turanConjectureK43 = 5/9 ≈ 0.556** is the conjectured density. The Turán hypergraph T(n,4,3) — obtained by partitioning n vertices into 4 balanced parts and taking 3-edges meeting at least 2 parts — achieves this density and is K_4^3-free.

**K43_lower_bound:** π_3(K_4^3) ≥ 5/9 (from the construction).
**K43_upper_bound_razborov:** π_3(K_4^3) ≤ 0.5616 (Razborov, flag algebras, 2010).

The gap between 5/9 ≈ 0.556 and 0.5616 is one of the most stubborn gaps in combinatorics.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of the k_4^3 case: turán's conjecture

title: Known Bounds and Methods
content:
**de_caen_lower_bound:** π_r(K_k^r) ≥ 1 - C(k-1,r)/C(k,r), giving non-trivial lower bounds for all cases.

**kruskal_katona_upper:** π_r(K_k^r) ≤ 1 - 1/k from the Kruskal-Katona theorem on shadows of set systems.

**flag_algebras_upper:** Razborov's method (2007) gives upper bounds strictly below Kruskal-Katona for specific cases using semidefinite programming on local density constraints.
mathContext: Flag algebras systematically exploit local density constraints to derive global bounds. While powerful, they have not closed any gap to an exact value for r > 2.

title: Erdős Problem #712: Main Theorem
content:
**erdos_712** is the main entry-point theorem, FULLY PROVEN from the axioms. It establishes two facts:

1. The Turán density exists with 0 < π < 1 (using turan_density_positive and kruskal_katona_upper)
2. The exact value is unknown (using erdos_712_open)

The proof of π < 1 uses the Kruskal-Katona bound and positivity of k. This is one of the few theorems with actual tactic proofs (calc, linarith, positivity).

title: Related Conjectures
content:
**extremal_structure_conjecture:** For each r, k, the extremal hypergraph should be 'nice' — specifically, a balanced k-partition construction analogous to the Turán graph. This is unproven for any r > 2.

**mubayi_K53_conjecture:** π_3(K_5^3) = 3/4, the next simplest case after K_4^3.
